# Review: the Rust doc comments for the Python reader

This document reports backlog item 0310.[^1] The item writes the prose that the
published Python reference carries, and it removes the copies of that prose from
the type stub.

## 1. The impact review

The item arrived in `proposed/`. This section is the review that moved it to
`refined/`, and the item file now carries the same answers.[^1]

**Governed by.** One record binds the work, and it holds four decisions.[^2]

**D1, the reference is generated by an import of the compiled module.** This
item implements nothing of D1. It writes into the bindings crate, which is what
the import reads. A separate item owns the build.[^3]

**D2, the prose of a member the module provides lives in the Rust doc comment
and nowhere else.** This is what the item implements. Every word written here
went into the bindings crate.[^4] Nothing went into a documentation page.

**D3, the stub declares types and carries prose only for a declaration the
module does not provide.** The item implements the removal half of D3. Eleven
docstrings in the stub copied the Rust source, and a finding holds the
evidence.[^5] All eleven are gone. The typed dictionaries keep their prose,
because the module provides no counterpart for any of them.

**D4, the job builds the extension before it builds the site.** Not this item.
The site item owns the job.[^3]

**Changes.** No record. The work contradicts no decision.

**Creates.** No record. The test for whether a decision needs a record fails at
its first statement: no future contributor could reasonably decide that a doc
comment should not say what a call returns.[^6]

**Blockers.** None governs the work itself. Two govern what the prose may say.
One holds every cost figure, and no doc comment written here states a
performance number.[^7] One asks whether an upgrade changes hands when the
ground under it does, and no public member of the module reaches that
behaviour, so nothing had to cite it.[^8]

**Precedent.** Four findings shaped the work. The type stub once claimed a
generator and a check that do not exist.[^9] The package docstring once said the
verb interface was unwritten while a verb ran.[^10] The orientation document
sells a pyramid level that nothing writes, and an agent server that the package
never installs.[^11] [^12] Every claim written here was checked against the
source or against a run of the built module before it was written.

## 2. What was documented

The module holds twelve public names: the `World` class, the `Camera` class, the
`version` function and nine error classes. Every one now carries prose written
for a Python reader.

**The module docstring is new prose, and it is the front page.** The binding
library makes the doc comment of the module function the docstring of the
module, so a reader who lands on the reference sees it first. It read "Builds
the extension module." That is a sentence about a Rust function, and it told the
Python reader nothing.

It now states five conventions, so that each member below can rely on them.

1. A fixed-point value crosses as a raw integer at a scale of 65536.
2. An entity crosses as one opaque unsigned 64-bit identity, and a stale one
   raises rather than answers.
3. A tile crosses either as an axial address or as a row-major index, and the
   conversion between them is given.
4. A resource kind, a ground kind and a faction each cross as a small integer,
   and the numbering of each is named.
5. Python sends one command over a set, a set-valued verb is all or nothing,
   and nothing in the module enforces the rule.

**Every method, property and error class.** For each one the reader now learns
what it does, what each argument means, what Python type comes back, in what
unit each numeric entry is expressed, and which class the call raises. Each
returned mapping is documented entry by entry, with the NumPy element type where
the entry is an array.

**The error classes carry the case that raises them.** The root class also
states the three built-in classes that the binding raises before a call reaches
the engine, because none of the three is a subclass of the root and a caller
that catches only the root does not catch them.

## 3. What was deliberately left undocumented

**No cost figure and no performance claim.** One blocker holds every figure in
this project.[^7] The frame report carries three floating point entries that
measure a machine, and the doc comment says plainly that they measure the
machine and not the simulation.

**No default value that a tuning change would move.** The rebalance schedule has
a default period. The doc comment says that the world starts with a schedule and
that the call replaces it, and it states no number.

**No count of the members of the module.** A count in prose goes stale on the
next member added.

**Nothing about ownership of an upgrade when the ground changes hands.** The
question is open.[^8] No public member reaches the behaviour.

**The private helper functions of the crate.** They are Rust, and the Rust
reader is a different audience that the product record excludes.[^13]

## 4. How the fixed-point values were handled

The engine holds no floating point number in simulated state, and the scale is
Q16.16.[^14] A caller that reads such an integer as a quantity is wrong by a
factor of 65536, and nothing reports it.

Three things were done.

**The scale is stated once at the top, in full.** The module docstring says what
Q16.16 is, gives the number 65536, and says to divide to read and to multiply to
write.

**Every entry that carries the scale names it where the reader meets it.** A
reader lands on one member of a generated reference, not on the front page, so
the repetition is what keeps each member readable on its own. The rule permits
the repetition for that reason.[^15]

**The mixed cases are called out.** The summary of a region is the sharp one.
Its value total and its height total are Q16.16 raw integers, and its food total
is a whole count of stock. The stub described all three as raw accumulator
integers, which is true and useless. Both the doc comment and the stub now say
which two scale and which one does not, and both warn that a reader who scales
all three reports a food total 65536 times too small.

The scale was verified by running the built module, not by reading the source
alone. A region of 256 tiles reported a height total of 8833542, which is 0.53
for each tile after division, and a food total of 270, which is about one unit
for each tile without division.

The founding score is the second case. It is an `int64`, and the stub called it
"an exact integer". It is a Q16.16 raw integer, and both sites now say so.

## 5. The duplicate prose removed from the stub

The finding names eleven copies: nine exception docstrings that agree with the
Rust strings word for word, one `World` class docstring, and one `Camera` class
docstring that is an abridged copy which dropped the paragraph warning against
one value in two places.[^5]

All eleven are gone. The eleven classes now carry types and no prose. The nine
error classes are one line each.

The stub's own module docstring said that the copies below it were a defect the
backlog would remove. That sentence is now false, so it was replaced by a
sentence that states what the file holds today and cites the finding for what
the copies were.

**The sweep is complete, and a derived check proves it.** A grep is not enough,
because the question is not "does a docstring exist" but "does a docstring exist
on a declaration the module provides". The check parses the stub, walks every
class and function, and asks the imported module for a member of that name.

```
uv run python - <<'EOF'
import ast, pathlib, cachette._core as core
tree = ast.parse(pathlib.Path("python/cachette/_core.pyi").read_text())
bad = []
for node in ast.walk(tree):
    if not isinstance(node, (ast.ClassDef, ast.FunctionDef)):
        continue
    if ast.get_docstring(node) and getattr(core, node.name, None) is not None:
        bad.append(node.name)
    for child in getattr(node, "body", []):
        if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef) and ast.get_docstring(child):
            bad.append(f"{node.name}.{child.name}")
print(bad)
assert not bad, bad
EOF
```

It prints an empty list. Every docstring that stays belongs to a typed
dictionary, and the module provides none of those.

## 6. The false claims found

**Three error classes are inert.** Nothing raises `SelectorError`, nothing
raises `DeterminismError`, and nothing raises `EnginePanic`. Each appears twice
in the whole tree: at its declaration and at its registration. A Rust panic at
the boundary raises the binding library's own panic class, which is not a
subclass of the root error class, so the promise the panic class makes is not
kept by anything. The finding holds the evidence and the search command.[^16]
The three docstrings now say that nothing raises them.

**A refused faction names the wrong bound.** The world checks the faction
against its own faction count, and reports the refusal through the arena's
ceiling error, which formats a different constant. A world with a faction count
of one refuses the faction three and says that three is at or above 63. The
finding holds it.[^17] The message is engine text, so it is not repaired here.

**A tile does not refuse a unit above its capacity, and a draft of this work
said it did.** The claim was written into the spawn doc comment, then checked
against the record and against a run. Twenty soldiers went onto one tile whose
capacity is eight, and the engine accepted every one. A record states that a
spawn may over-fill a tile and that only movement enforces the capacity.[^18]
The doc comment now states the record's answer.

**The stub declared one entry of the frame report as a tuple, and the module
returns a list.** The `carried_by_kind` entry is a Python list. Nothing failed,
because nothing compares the stub against the module, which is the finding that
is already on file.[^9] The declaration is corrected to `list[int]`.

## 7. The gates

Every gate below was run from the worktree of this item. The Rust source
changed, so the Rust gates ran as well as the Python ones.

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rust formatting | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | passed, no output |
| Rust lint | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | passed, no warning |
| Python formatting | `uv run ruff format --check python tests` | 46 files already formatted |
| Python lint | `uv run ruff check python tests` | All checks passed |
| Types | `uv run mypy` | Success: no issues found in 18 source files |
| Python tests | `uv run pytest` | 74 passed |
| Rust tests | `cargo test --workspace` | passed inside `just check` |
| Records | `just records` | 71 records, 21 product records, 215 backlog items, 362 register entries, 161 priority rows, 5969 citations, 371 documents of footnotes: 0 failures |
| Whole gate | `just check` | exit code 0 |

`just check` runs the formatting check, the lint, the invariant scripts, every
Rust and Python test, the record checks, the probe that proves each record
check can fail, and the merge-defect check. It exited zero.

The record check reports two notes that it does not fail on. ADR-0082 and
ADR-0097 are cited by no other record and no source file, and both notes
predate this work.

**The gate suite is over its local time budget, and the wrapper reports that
without failing.** The figure describes a development machine and is not
evidence about the target platform. This work added no gate.

## 8. What was left undone

**The two defects found are not repaired.** The three inert error classes stay
declared, and the faction refusal still names the wrong bound. Both are engine
work, and the item forbids a behaviour change.

**The reference page was not read, because no page exists.** The item as
proposed said to read the generated page and repair what it showed. The site
item had not published one when this ran.[^3] The module was imported instead,
and every docstring the import creates was read from the built module, which is
the same source the page is generated from. That reaches the same members. It
does not show how the page renders them, and in particular it does not show the
repeated heading problem that the record names in its own consequences.[^2]

**The heading level of a docstring section was not chosen.** The record says the
project either chooses one or accepts the repetition of the references heading
and the errors heading down a long page. Every doc comment written here follows
the project rule and carries both, so the page will repeat them. That is a
choice for the site item, which can see the rendering.
